newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - dealers.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Midwest hog prices seen steady-firm - dealers.

text.p: Midwest direct cash hog prices Tuesday were seen steady with a firm tone, amid expectations for lighter hog marketings, livestock dealers said.

Top prices in the Iowa and southern Minnesota markets for hogs delivered at plants could range from $58.00 to $58.50 dollars per cwt while Illinois top prices at plants could range from $57.50 to $58.00.
Indiana top prices could range from $57.50 to $58.00 and Ohio tops were seen at $54.00 to $55.00, dealers there said.
Hog prices could be underpinned Tuesday by lighter hog marketings in the Midwest as warm, dry weather starts providing opportunities for producers to pick up harvest activities, the dealers said.
But support from expected lighter hog marketings could be offset by reticent packer demand if pork prices remain weak by the end of the day, market sources said.

At midday, carlot pork was trading slowly, with hams generally $1.00 per cwt lower and lean trimmings weak, according to USDA. There were 12.5 fabricated loads and 8.0 loads of trimmings reported sold.
